name: Painted in the Suzhou manner (苏式彩画)
process: Architectural painting on beams and boards over a 地仗 ground: mineral pigments in a glue binder laid flat in bands and panels, with a 包袱 (a large 'wrapper' panel of landscape, figures or flowers) at the middle of each bay's beams, and 箍头 bands at the ends; details in gold leaf over a mordant. Matt where the pigment lies bare; the gilding catches the light.

design.text: 苏式彩画: azurite, malachite, gold leaf; a painted 包袱 in each bay of the house beams.

pattern: The painted image is an atlas the stage draws (the first build's T_ch_suhua, generated by windows/Scripts/chenghuai_textures.py): a design artefact, not evidence.

surface.finish: Dead matt pigment fields (coarse mineral particles in glue), a slight relief at band edges, bright gold.

photograph: Flat blue and green bands with crisp white and black outlines; the 包袱 panel a picture framed in the beam; gold catching light at the edges.
Old work: powdery, faded where weathered, dark with soot under eaves, flaking at cracks.

unverified.reason: Glue (animal glue) as the pigment binder is the trade's account; no source describing the binder of 苏式彩画 was read (Huang et al. found protein and tung oil in the ground).
Coarse azurite and malachite grades set the colour; sizes were not read.
